page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with marginal notes in the right margin (several beside the verse quotations and one at the foot of the text block). Running head at top; signature and catchword at the foot. The left edge shows part of the facing page, which is not transcribed.

main_text.p: de iis Ioui consecrasset. Sed satis de loricis hamatis. ad quas referendi Statiani versus isti:

Iterum: ——magnorumque area suta Lib. iii.
Thoracum. Et tertium:

Vbi suta haec appellat, siue catenas iunctas, siue laminas Trilices lorica. nexas, vtrum voles. Ait & in extremis versibus ter insutum ferrum: vt ostendat trilicem loricam eam fuisse. id est, catenas aut laminas sic geminatas. Sic in Virgilio:

In Valerio: Per clypei cedentis opus, partemque trilicem. Lib.ii. In Silio: ——textam nodis auroque trilicem Lib.ii.
Loricam.
Etsi haec postrema ad lineam loricam fas sit & tranferri.

At de squamis etiam geminis Virgilius:
Nec duplici squama lorica fidelis & auro Lib. ix.
Sustinuit.

Atque hic talis textus an non Crates in Statio?
Omnibus ærat & propugnant pectora crates. Lib.iiii.
Item Silio: ——clypeo stetit [?] aris in ora Lib.v.
Cuspis, & oppositas vt ita est transmittere crates.

An clypeorum * Supra de iis, Dial. ii.* crates intellegunt, quibus coria indu-cta [?], & vmbo ex ære aut ferro? An potius, vt dixi, has loricas, in quibus anulorum ordines & textus velut crates referunt? An denique aliud genus, quod Statij & Silij Lorica segmentata. æuo crebrum? cùm segmenta ferrea, tamquam fasciæ aliæ aliis superpositæ, corpus ambiunt. page.notes: Marginal notes are placed at the lines they stand beside. The asterisk in the text after "clypeorum" carries the note "* Supra de iis, Dial. ii." on the right. The note "Lorica segmentata." sits at the line of "Silij" and "æuo"; its side is the right margin, so the side attribute should read right, not left. Doubtful readings: "stetit" (the printed letter looks like "sletit" or "fletit"), "ærat" in "Omnibus ærat", "indu-cta" (the ligature is unclear), and the italic "suta" forms. The word after "Silio" in the Silius verse may be misprinted or unclear. Show-through and the facing page's edge at the left are excluded.
